A string instrument with a teardrop-shaped body and two strings, played with a bow, originating in Tuvan folk music.
A large, double-sided Tuvan drum, often made of goatskin and adorned with bells, introduced by Tibetan Buddhists.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tuvan кеңгирге (keñgirge). Compare Mongolian хэнгэрэг (xengereg) and several other cognates.

parole.significato: A style of throat singing, often accompanied by the horsehead fiddle, from Mongolia and eastern Siberia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tuvan хөөмей (xöömey) and Mongolian хөөмий (xöömii), ᠬᠥᠭᠡᠮᠡᠢ (kögemei).
